featured_reviews.name: Ritesh K R
featured_reviews.review_text:
Kondivite Caves (Mahakali Caves) are one of Mumbai’s most underrated historical gems—quiet, raw, and deeply rooted in India’s ancient Buddhist past.

Dating back to around the 2nd century BCE, these rock-cut caves began in the Hinayana tradition and later saw influences of the Mahayana phase, remaining active up to around the 6th century CE and even beyond till the 12th century in some form. You can actually sense this long continuity as you walk through the caves—simple early structures evolving into more developed spaces.

Carved out of basalt rock and once surrounded by dense forests, the setting would have been ideal for monks—isolated, peaceful, and close to natural water sources. Like Bhaje and Karle caves, the site reflects how geography and trade routes shaped spiritual centres.

The presence of Pali inscriptions adds another layer of authenticity and historical depth, connecting you directly to the lives and practices of the monks who once lived here.

Today, the caves still carry a quiet, meditative energy, though the surroundings could definitely be cleaner and better maintained. More signage or guided interpretation would really help visitors appreciate the historical context.

Overall, a fascinating visit—especially if you enjoy history, archaeology, or simply discovering hidden layers of Mumbai beyond its modern chaos.

featured_reviews.name: Abhijeet Thigale
featured_reviews.review_text:
The Mahakali Caves (historically known as the Kondivite Caves) are a hidden archaeological treasure tucked away in the bustle of Andheri East, Mumbai.
​Whether you're a history buff or just looking for a pocket of peace in the city, here is a review of this ancient site.
​The Experience: A Step Back in Time
​The Mahakali Caves are a group of 19 rock-cut Buddhist monuments dating from the 1st Century BCE to the 6th Century CE. Carved directly into solid black basalt rock, these caves served as a quiet retreat for Buddhist monks long before Mumbai became a financial hub.
​The Architecture
​Cave 9 (The Main Attraction): This is the largest and most significant cave. It features a Chaitya (prayer hall) with a stupa and a unique semicircular wall. Look closely at the walls—even though they have weathered over 2,000 years, you can still see mutilated figures of Buddha and characters from Buddhist mythology.
​The Viharas: The other caves are mostly Viharas (monasteries). These are small, stark cells where monks lived and meditated. Their simplicity is a powerful contrast to the modern skyscrapers visible in the distance.
​The View: Located on a small hill, the site offers a panoramic view of the Jogeshwari-Vikhroli Link Road (JVLR). It’s a surreal experience to stand in a 2,000-year-old monastery while watching the "maximum city" rush by below.

featured_reviews.name: Anika Mukerjee
featured_reviews.review_text:
As an eighteen-year-old who never enjoyed even the mere idea of a safari, I can honestly say that Mahek from Hiss and Croak has completely changed my perspective.

Organising a trip for a group of seven with two senior citizens couldn't have been easy to manage but Mahek executed and planned everything perfectly. From the accommodation to the actual safaris, every single aspect was taken care of so we could all relax and enjoy our trip to the max.

We did a total of six safaris and were fortunate enough to see eleven tigers— some multiple times— and several other animals including, but not limited to, various kinds of deer, gaur, and even a bear with her cub.

The highlight of the trip had to be when we witnessed the tiger Choti Tara and her two cubs strategically hunt and kill a deer. It was truly surreal to witness nature at its rawest form, and from not even fifty feet away.

Thank you so much, Mahek and Hiss and Croak for the trip of a lifetime and this unforgettable experience.

Strongly recommended Hiss & Croak for amazing safari experiences.

We have promised her that we will visit again.

Chitra Sridhar
Muscat

I had booked this car for Mumbai Darshan for my inlaws with the package of 12hr/120 Kms. They have mentioned on their website to show 26 places and committed the same. We have asked for 9am but driver arrived at 9:30am. Their policy says full refund if driver does not report on time. After asking there was no response. They said he will come from Vashi but he was actually coming from Andheri. While booking they mentioned that they have 7 years experience of the same travel. I booked this for Monday and found out later that some places like Nehru Planetarium and Aquarium are closed on Monday. I asked them why you never mentioned about it. They said even they are not aware of this; in 7 years  they did not find this out. So the journey started at 9:30 am from Airoli. My wife already told him that excluding closed places and some not interested to see these 20 places we want to see so manage the tour accordingly. Driver was converset with the locality and agreed to do so. Driver was literally sleeping while driving. My wife suggested to pull over and take a nap or drive slowly. He did neither and kept on driving. We have had already lost some time so she thought he will take the rest we will go to Sidhivinayak and avoided to call travel company to save on time. His drowsiness  was all the day of the travel. He skipped some places saying we will need to go back and miss some points. He was travelling through the places but not at all telling that Worli sea link is at your right or Mantralaya building was at you left, nothing like that. After asking he used to say it just passed by (Abhi to peechhe gaya). Now my family did not know where it is the reason we booked the car and he did not take any efforts to mention them. Overall it was just the travel with 13 places (including these abhi peechhe gaya places) out of 20 places and my family was traumatized by his driving. After reaching home I asked him why he was sleeping, he rudely said that he was feeling lazy (Susti aa rahi thi sir). And also asked why he did not show the places then he said I needed to go tru and fro and also I thought these people already know where is what again very rudely. I talked with travel company then they said they are vendors and will be penalized for this behavior. But what about us we just spent a day in the car without seeing anything and paid in full. Also there was risk as driver was sleepy. I had to again book a self drive car and have to show the places again to my in-laws.
I did not get any notification about the reply. And there is no option to reply to your comment. The commitment was to provide from Vashi if it was not available then that is not my fault. I checked there was no accident. Also he reached in Airoli at 8:55 as per the phone discussion but he was touring inside for 30 min. I called up even in the evening when the driver reached back home but there was no such information provided that I need to speak to customer care. Even the person on the other side mentioned that you guys will be penalising the vendor and will let me know what happens.
